findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded-post metadata link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: In the diff for .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a, the old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70%, so on light themes this link becomes much lighter than before — dark-light-choose is supposed to preserve the existing light value and only add the dark variant. This looks like a copy/paste of the complementary values into the wrong branch and will visibly regress light themes.

findings.title: topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.body: The mobile .topic-map h3 rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 20% to 50%, making the heading noticeably lighter on light themes; the conversion should have kept 20% for the light branch (e.g. paired with 80% on the dark branch, as done for .number/i a few lines below).

findings.title: custom-message-length light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness
findings.body: .custom-message-length was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme branch went from 70% to 30%, so the character-count hint text becomes much darker on light themes. The two values appear to have been swapped; the desktop version of the same rule uses (70%, 30%) correctly.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: In desktop/user.scss the .group-member-info .name rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, unintentionally lightening group member names on light themes (the mobile version of the same rule in mobile/user.scss has the same change). The light branch should have preserved the original 30%.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: In mobile/user.scss the .group-member-info .name rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme rendering rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. The original 30% lightness should be kept for the light branch.
